Marsileaceae.key_door: rooted aquatic/amphibious fern + long petiole + four-part clover-like blade + hard sporocarp containing both micro- and megaspores

Salviniaceae.key_door: tiny free-floating branched fern + overlapping bilobed leaves + hanging roots + micro- and megasporocarps

taxonomy_notes: Marsilea macropoda and Marsilea vestita remain accepted current species concepts.
Marsilea vestita subsp. tenuifolia is retained only as synonym provenance for accepted M. vestita under current Kew.
Azolla caroliniana remains accepted under current Kew and native range includes Texas.

Flora of North America uses Azollaceae for Azolla; current Kew treats Azollaceae as a synonym of Salviniaceae. Project uses current Salviniaceae while preserving older Azollaceae as searchable provenance.
field_guardrails: Do not identify project Marsilea to species from leaves alone; fertile sporocarps carry the strongest characters.
FNA reports M. macropoda × M. vestita intermediates/putative hybrids in Blanco County, inside the project target zone.
Do not force sterile Azolla to species from color or mat appearance; reliable species separation may require sporocarps and microscopy.
Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
lineage_lesson: Both Salviniales families are heterosporous aquatic ferns. Marsileaceae is the rooted four-leaflet, hard-sporocarp branch; Salviniaceae/Azolla is the tiny free-floating bilobed-leaf branch.
